root_cause: Read-only specialist lane (oracle) tasked with producing a deliverable JSON payload that must persist; no persistence plan at dispatch time; orchestrator assumed the payload would survive in the lane's ephemeral response buffer. Recurrence on 2026-07-31 (ora-9) showed the corrective action was documentation-only: it specified the rule but added no close-time enforcement gate, and the lane returned a status-only message with no payload.
corrective_action: When dispatching a write-required deliverable to a read-only lane, either (a) require the full payload inside the returned task result text, or (b) have the lane write to a permitted path, or (c) if neither is possible, dispatch a write-capable lane (fixer). Verify payload capture BEFORE lane close.
verification: First closure validated on TICKET-005 (ora-5 persisted to %TEMP%\opencode\l4_antihypertensive.json; merged 49/49, spot-check APPROVE). REOPENED 2026-07-31 for recurrence (ora-9: no payload in result). New enforcement added: orchestrator close-time gate (process-mappings.md) — before declaring a read-only lane reconciled, confirm the required payload keys are present in the returned task result; if absent, re-dispatch immediately without marking reconciled.
prevention: Orchestrator dispatch + close checklist (process-mappings.md, section 1): (1) at dispatch, state the persistence mechanism (disk path OR full payload in result); (2) at close, verify payload presence in the returned result BEFORE marking the lane reconciled; (3) on absence, re-dispatch with the same objective and do not close the lane. Applies to oracle, explorer, librarian, designer, verifier lanes.
